artefacts.description: The machine-readable documentation index — the entry point.
A compact brief for AI coding agents: what to import, what to catch, what not to write.
llms.txt, the README and every guide in one text.
Every executable recipe, fenced as TypeScript.
The public surface: every export with module, signature, summary and thrown error classes.
Every error code with its class, cause, remedy, standard and CWE.
Every diagnostic code with its severity, cause, remedy and standard.
The named resource limits with their defaults and CWE.
What pkinative does, the exports, CLI commands and MCP tools that do it, and since which version.
The playgrounds: what each runs, its controls by DOM id, and the exports, command lines or tools it drives.
The pkinative-cli command surface — commands, flags, exit codes, error classes — from its own capability manifest.
Versions, milestones, contracts, corpus pins and counts — the single source of truth.

guides.title: Quick start
guides.summary: Read a certificate in three calls, then learn the four things every pkinative call shares: strict DER, typed errors, diagnostics and limits. Everything below runs on pkinative 1.0 as it is tested; every export named here is in docs/assets/api.json.

guides.title: Use cases
guides.summary: The jobs pkinative does today, with the code that does them and the guarantee behind each. Four need no signature at all; the rest check and write signatures, validate chains, ask about revocation, sign, verify and timestamp CMS messages, and open the PKCS#8 keys and PKCS#12 files that sign them.

guides.title: pkinative-cli — Command-line reference
guides.summary: pkinative-cli 1.0.0 puts the whole pkinative engine on the command line: 18 commands, offline, with a stable --json contract for scripts, CI and AI agents. It pins pkinative ^1.0.0, its only runtime dependency.

guides.title: CLI use cases
guides.summary: Four pipelines built from the pkinative-cli samples: a CI gate on a chain and its expiry, revocation checked offline, a signed and timestamped release, and a PKCS#12 audit. Every command below is one a sample runs, or a flag the CLI guide documents.

guides.title: pkinative-mcp — AI client integration
guides.summary: pkinative-mcp 1.0.0 gives AI assistants the pkinative engine as 34 typed tools, seven prompts and sandboxed file resources, over stdio or loopback Streamable HTTP, with no network access, ever. It pins pkinative ^1.0.0.

guides.title: MCP use cases
guides.summary: Four conversations built from the pkinative-mcp examples and prompts: triaging a failing TLS chain, issuing a test certificate, checking revocation offline, and opening keys without leaking a byte.

guides.title: Security model
guides.summary: Every certificate, PEM text and DER blob pkinative reads is treated as attacker-controlled. This guide explains what that means in practice: strict decoding, bounded resources, typed failures, and a hard line around cryptography.

guides.title: Conformance
guides.summary: pkinative is held to corpora it did not write and to parsers it does not share code with. A blocking gate runs the built package over x509-limbo and Wycheproof, pinned by commit and SHA-256, and compares serial, validity, CA flag and fingerprint with OpenSSL.

guides.title: Standards
guides.summary: A tooled self-assessment, not a certification. Every ISO/IEC, ITU-T and IETF standard pkinative touches, the evidence that holds each — a test, a rule or a conformance level — and the gaps it leaves.

guides.title: Errors, diagnostics and reasons
guides.summary: Every failure has a stable code, and every code has a cause and a remedy. Branch on the code; the message is for people. The machine-readable registries are docs/data/errors.json, docs/data/diagnostics.json and docs/data/reasons.json.

guides.title: Choosing a PKI library
guides.summary: Choose pkinative for strict, dependency-free PKI in any JavaScript runtime — certificates, paths and revocation, CMS and timestamps, PKCS#8 and PKCS#12 — with every refusal explained by a stable code. Choose another tool for what it will never do, listed below.
